Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case `testStop2` in `PosixParserTest` failed because the `PosixParser` does not handle unrecognized tokens starting with '-' properly when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. In this case, when the option 'a' is not set and the command line `"-z -a foo"` is provided, the parser interprets it as `"-a foo"`, ignoring the unrecognized token '-z'.

Looking at the recent bug reports, there are similar issues reported with `PosixParser` not stopping parsing on certain tokens or characters. This indicates a recurring pattern of incorrect behavior in token parsing and recognition.

To confirm the root cause, we need to inspect the implementation of the `PosixParser` class.

I will retrieve relevant code snippets for the `PosixParser` class to further analyze the issue.

messages.content:
The `PosixParser` class has a method `process(String value)` where the processing of tokens occurs. In this method, if the current option requires an argument, the value is added to the token list. However, there is a condition where if the current option does not require an argument, it sets `eatTheRest` to true and adds `--` followed by the value to the tokens list.

This behavior explains why when an unrecognized token starting with '-' is encountered, it is being added to the tokens list along with the rest of the values.

To fix this issue, we need to update the `process(String value)` method in the `PosixParser` class to handle unrecognized tokens starting with '-' properly when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. By modifying this method to skip adding unrecognized tokens to the token list, we can ensure that only recognized options and their arguments are processed.

The fix should be applied in:
`org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.process(java.lang.String)`

Next, I will provide the best locations to apply these fixes.
`org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.process(java.lang.String)`
